I'm going to sound like a commercial but this is what I personally use. Here are your steps. You'll need about $50 for up front. After this you'll save money like a motherfucker.

  1. Run down to Walgreen's or some other place like that. Walgreen's was where I found mine. Buy a MicroTouch One (The Safety Razor) Yeah, the As Seen On TV one. Get it. It comes with ten blades and a stand for your razor.

  2. Buy the Van Der Hagen Shave set. It comes with a mug, soap, brush and a stand for the brush. All of this will cost you up to about $50 or so.

  3. Put the soap in the mug

  4. Get the brush wet

  5. Start brushing the soap until it lathers up

  6. Apply soap to wherever you want to shave

  7. Put a blade in the safety razor

  8. Shave...carefully until you're used to it

Here's the thing about Safety razors and the single blade thing. There's a slight learning curve. It's not as quick and easy as the disposables or cartridge driven razors. It also takes just a tad longer until you're used to it. If you shave your head like I do, there's a real learning curve. The trick I learned it that, if it feels like you're scraping hair off of you, you're doing it right. Slow and steady, rinse often. Don't go over the same patches more than maybe once or twice or your skin is going to be burning like a son of a bitch. Try to find a cooling aftershave if you can.

Once you get used to it, aftershave is a take it or leave it kinda thing. It is for me. The blades will last a hell of a long time. I've bought blades...maybe once in the two years I've been using this system. I've bought a cake of soap once. Granted I might shave once a week at most but there it is. The soap is about five bucks, the foams and gels do absolutely nothing. You need the soap to soften the hair because it does it best. Blades cost about five bucks for a pack of five, they're cheaper if you buy them from Dorco.com in bulk. Let me tell you, once you get the hang of it, closest...smoothest...shave...ever. I've always wanted to take a photo of my shave set and do one of those overhyped marketing memes with it sorta like this

Safety razors are the way to go if you keep a clean shaven face on the regular.

One more thing to add is to have a mason jar of rubbing alcohol to dip the blades in after use. It evaporates the water on the blade, thereby slowing down the microscopic rust that dulls the blade.

Basically, dip razors in rubbing alcohol to extend their life span.
